statement: If two triangular arrangement faces share lines i,j and their remote vertices lie on the same ray of shared line i from P_ij, those remote vertices coincide; therefore i and the two third lines are concurrent. The analogous implication holds on j.
proof: Each face side from P_ij to its remote vertex contains no arrangement vertex in its relative interior. On one ray, two distinct remote vertices are linearly ordered, so the nearer would lie in the farther face side. Hence the vertices are equal, which is exactly the required triple concurrency.

clause_schema: and the two analogous clauses on shared line j
